status_note: Registered on 2026-11-27 before any perplexity of this comparison was measured. THME-2206, ROADMAP v0.2.2.6.

evaluation.scoring_note: Full test split in consecutive windows of 1024 (thme evaluate defaults), same protocol as the verification reports.

comparators.note: Read from that file, not re-run.

unrotated.description: The same 15 symmetric levels (k/7, k = -7..7) and absolute-maximum scale as thme.hadamard_int4, with no rotation; defined in this protocol as a custom algorithm

preregistration.registered_before: any measured perplexity of this comparison
decision_rule: Every arm is deterministic (no calibration data, no seed), so there is no run-to-run variance; a relative threshold is used instead.

Within a pair, rotation is better if the rotated perplexity is lower than the unrotated one by at least 1 percent of the unrotated perplexity, worse if higher by at least 1 percent, otherwise no difference is shown.
Gate: reported for the repository default (v1, at most 0.45 above the ceiling) and read from the `thme evaluate` report; nothing is judged by the gate here.
A null or negative result is a valid result and is reported as one. The 1 percent threshold, the pairs and this rule are fixed here and are not changed after any measured result is seen.
limits: Both rotated rules use blocks of 64 weights; no other block size is tried.
The int4 pair compares a rule defined in this protocol with the built-in rotated rule; the rotation is the only difference.
One corpus, one model per file; no calibration-based arm.

results.reading: Rotation is better by the pre-registered 1 percent rule in both pairs on SmolLM-135M (int4 7,318,545 to 466,209; ternary 75,358,699 to 28,581,957), but every arm is unusable against the ceiling of 19.80, and on Pythia-14M the int4 pair went the other way (rotation worse), so rotation is not a consistent improvement. These codebooks use one absolute-maximum scale for the whole tensor, which destroys these small models with or without rotation.
results.device_note: All four arms ran on THME's CUDA path (embedded PTX) on 27 November 2026; the Pythia-14M file used the CPU. Results are not mixed across devices inside one file.
